m1 - INDEPENDENT RE-DERIVATION ON 244257d: ALL SIX NUMBERS CONFIRMED EXACTLY. I built a clean detached worktree at your SHA, computed the quantities myself rather than reading your assertions, then destroyed the worktree.

  chronology   value 0.039516  support 0.304620  cond 0.913861  total 3.000000
  specificity  massWeighted 0.678220  meanOfRatios 0.628359  cond 2.736038

DISCRIMINATOR IS LIVE, which was the thing I most wanted checked: per-unit source masses are 0.7424, 0.0832, 0.9955, 0.9150 - four distinct values out of four, so the unequal-mass requirement holds - and the formula gap is 0.049861, comfortably above the 1e-9 the test demands. Stemming did not equalise source mass, so the assertion the whole compression/specificity ruling rests on is still discriminating rather than vacuous.

THE DERIVATION SHAPE IS RIGHT. Deriving lemmas through Lexical.stems from raw human-readable inputs, rather than hand-writing the stemmed forms, is better than what I would have done - it makes future stemmer changes propagate instead of silently drifting, which is the actual disease.

ONE REVIEW FINDING, AND ONE THING I ALMOST GOT WRONG.

The finding: AnnaFixtureSuite's first test computes `expected` with `terms.flatMap(Lexical.stems).toSet` and compares it to nodes built with `terms.iterator.flatMap(Lexical.stems).toSet`. Those are the same expression, so the test pins the WIRING - that nodes actually use nodeLemmasFrom over nodeLemmaInputs, which is worth pinning - but it cannot fail for any change to Lexical.stems itself. If the stemmer became the identity function tomorrow, both sides would move together, the test would pass, and the fixture would be silently back to raw lemmas. That is the exact defect you just fixed, and the guard against it does not guard against it.

Suggested addition, one line, non-self-referential because it names a concrete value the stemmer must produce:

  assert(AnnaFixture.nodes.head.lemmas.contains("isol"))
  assert(!AnnaFixture.nodes.head.lemmas.contains("isolated"))

WHAT I ALMOST GOT WRONG, and why I am telling you instead of just sending the good version. My first instinct was to suggest asserting that every lemma equals its own stem - the check I used to FIND the original bug. I ran it against your tree before recommending it and it reports 2 of 21 lemmas failing: `hous` and `nois`. Not a defect in your change. THE STEMMER IS NOT IDEMPOTENT: stem("house") = "hous" but stem("hous") = "hou", and stem("nois") = "noi". So my proposed assertion would have failed on correct output. The Scaladoc claims idempotence only for the irregular table, not generally, so this is documented rather than broken.

BUT IT IS A HAZARD FOR YOUR DESIGN SPECIFICALLY: nodeLemmasFrom must never be applied to an already-derived lemma set. Doing it twice silently shortens every lemma and breaks all matching, with no error. If there is any chance a future caller composes it, consider taking raw inputs by a distinct type or naming it fromRawTerms so the mistake is visible at the call site.

No objection from me on the candidate. The pinned-value updates match my authorization and the numbers are mine to confirm, which I now have, independently.
